cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Aerodynamics studies the interaction between air and moving objects; it is critical for vehicle and aircraft design.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Drag is the aerodynamic force that opposes motion through air; it increases with the square of velocity (drag proportional to v2).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Thrust is the force that propels an object forward; it must overcome drag to maintain speed or accelerate.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Lift is the upward aerodynamic force that keeps aircraft airborne; it is generated by the pressure difference across an aerofoil.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Streamlining reduces drag by shaping an object so air flows smoothly around it with minimal turbulence and separation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Bernoulli's principle: faster-moving air has lower pressure; an aerofoil's curved upper surface speeds the air, creating lower pressure above than below, generating lift.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Drag coefficient (Cd) quantifies how aerodynamic a shape is: lower Cd means less drag for a given speed and frontal area.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Wind tunnel testing measures aerodynamic forces on scale models; smoke visualisation shows airflow patterns.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) simulates airflow digitally, allowing aerodynamic optimisation before physical testing.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Parasitic drag includes form drag (shape of object) and skin friction (surface roughness); both can be reduced by design.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Aerodynamic design in cars reduces fuel consumption and increases top speed; even small reductions in Cd have significant effects at high speed.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Aerodynamics in Engineering
cards.back: Downforce in racing cars uses inverted aerofoil principles to push the car onto the road, increasing grip for cornering.
